title: Elements, Compounds and Mixtures
seo_title: Secondary 1 Science: Elements, Compounds and Mixtures Worksheets with Answers
standard_code: Secondary 1: Exploring Diversity of Matter by its Chemical Composition
standard_text: Describe elements as the basic building blocks of matter and recognise metals and non-metals in the Periodic Table; describe compounds as two or more elements chemically combined and mixtures as substances not chemically combined; distinguish solute, solvent and solution, and solutions and suspensions; investigate factors that affect the rate of dissolving and solubility (summary of the MOE Lower Secondary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 1 science worksheets for Singapore students on elements, compounds and mixtures: metals and non-metals, chemical symbols, solutions, suspensions and solubility. With answers.
key_big: Compound: chemically combined. Mixture: not combined.
body_html:
How to think about it

All matter is made of elements. Elements combine to form compounds, or mix without combining to form mixtures.

  • Element: cannot be broken down chemically. Metals are on the left of the Periodic Table, non-metals on the right.
  • Compound: elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio; it has new properties (water, carbon dioxide).
  • Mixture: not chemically combined; can be separated physically (air, sea water).
  • A solute dissolves in a solvent to form a solution. Stirring, heat and smaller pieces dissolve a solid faster.
Example

Salt dissolves in water. Which is the solute?

The substance that dissolves

Answer: salt

Example

Iron and sulfur heated together form a black solid that is not magnetic. Element, compound or mixture?

New properties, cannot be separated by a magnet

Answer: a compound

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a compound keeps the properties of its elements.
  • Calling air a compound. It is a mixture of gases.
  • Mixing up the rate of dissolving and solubility. Stirring is faster, but the same mass dissolves.
  • Calling muddy water a solution. It is a suspension.

faq.q: What is the difference between a compound and a mixture?
faq.a: In a compound the elements are chemically combined in a fixed ratio and have new properties. In a mixture they are not combined and can be separated physically.

faq.q: What affects how fast a solid dissolves?
faq.a: Stirring, a higher temperature and smaller pieces (a larger surface area) make it dissolve faster.

faq.q: What is the difference between a solution and a suspension?
faq.a: A solution is clear and nothing settles. A suspension is cloudy; its particles settle and can be filtered out.
